title: Konosuba: God's Blessing on This Wonderful World!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shut-in gamer Kazuma Sato dies a humiliating death and is offered a new life in a fantasy world threatened by a Devil King; allowed one item, he picks the goddess Aqua herself (Yen Press blurb via AniList; ANN review). He forms a hapless party with Aqua, the explosion-obsessed wizard Megumin and the masochistic crusader Darkness in a comedy that parodies fantasy and isekai conventions (ANN; AniList Parody, Satire).
life_message: A messy, imperfect life with flawed friends is worth more than heroic glory; comfort and companionship are the real rewards.

content.note: Slapstick monster fights and comic deaths (ANN; AniList Slapstick).
Darkness's masochism and 'sexy swordswoman' (ANN); Ecchi, Harem genres and perverted male and female leads (MU); Female Harem (AniList); MangaDex suggestive.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Heroic honor is the joke; Kazuma avoids fights (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Kazuma wants comfort and freedom over quests (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: A found party of misfits, not blood family.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: A goddess reduced to a bickering equal (ANN; MU God-Human Relationship).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Fantasy and religious conventions parodied (AniList Parody, Satire).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Quality of life and indulgence over duty (ANN).

folkways.japan: Parodies the Japanese isekai boom and gamer otaku culture, including the hikikomori (shut-in) stereotype.

delivery.evidence: ANN reads it as parody with jokes that land; no lesson stated.
delivery.note: Satire works through gags rather than argument.

winners_losers: Nobody wins cleanly; the party muddles through. Sympathy goes to ordinary self-interest over heroic or divine pretensions.
